title: Alternating Sum, Forward Difference, and the One-Step Recurrence
content: `altSum a n m = ∑_{j∈Ico n m} (-1)^j a_j` is the alternating partial sum over the half-open window [n, m), and `fdiff a j = a_{j+1} − a_j` is the forward difference Δa_j. `altSum_succ` records the one-step recurrence altSum a n (m+1) = altSum a n m + (-1)^m a_m, an immediate consequence of Finset.sum_Ico_succ_top. Working over arbitrary windows Ico n m (rather than range m) is what makes the Boole identity reusable for tails of a series and what powers the Nat.le_induction proofs below.

title: First-Order Boole Summation Formula
content: `boole_first`: the exact identity altSum a n m = ½·((-1)^n a_n − (-1)^m a_m) − ½·altSum (Δa) n m. This is discrete summation by parts specialised to the alternating sign sequence: pairing (-1)^j against the antidifference of the signs collapses the sum into half its endpoint terms minus half the SAME alternating sum applied to the differences Δa. The leading endpoint term ½·(-1)^n a_n is exactly 'half the first term'. The proof is Nat.le_induction on m ≥ n: the base case m = n is the empty sum, and the successor step rewrites both alternating sums via altSum_succ, substitutes the inductive hypothesis and the definition of fdiff, and closes with ring (the sign flip (-1)^{m+1} = −(-1)^m is supplied by pow_succ).

title: Second-Order Iterate: the Δ²a Correction
content: `boole_second`: applying boole_first a second time, now to the differences Δa, exposes the discrete second-difference term altSum (Δ²a) n m with coefficient 1/4. This is the discrete analogue of the a'' term in the asymptotic expansion R_n ~ ((-1)^n/2)[a_n − (1/4)a_n'' + ⋯], and the start of the full Euler-number series. The proof simply rewrites with boole_first twice and calls ring — illustrating that the whole asymptotic expansion is generated by iterating one exact finite identity.

title: Exact Error Identity and Total-Variation Bound
content: `altSum_sub_half_endpoints` rearranges boole_first into the exact statement that the alternating sum minus its half-endpoint model equals −½·altSum (Δa) n m. Feeding this through the triangle inequality (`abs_altSum_le`, which uses |(-1)^j| = 1 so the signs drop out) gives `altSum_sub_half_endpoints_abs_le`: |altSum − model| ≤ ½∑|Δa_j|. The remainder of an alternating sum is thus controlled by half the total variation of a — a quantitative, hypothesis-light refinement of the Leibniz bound.

title: Half-First-Term Estimate for Decreasing Sequences
content: `sum_abs_fdiff_antitone` telescopes the total variation of a decreasing sequence: ∑_{j∈Ico n m} |Δa_j| = a_n − a_m (each |Δa_j| = a_j − a_{j+1} since a is antitone). Combined with the total-variation bound this yields `altSum_sub_half_first_le_antitone`: |altSum − model| ≤ ½(a_n − a_m). As the window's upper endpoint terms vanish (a_m → 0 for a convergent alternating series) the model collapses to ½·(-1)^n a_n and the bound to ½ a_n — the precise finite statement of 'the truncation remainder is approximately half the first omitted term'.
